name: Conceptual Physics / Hewitt Question-Family Profile
role: Course-specific question-structure benchmark layered beneath the current universal Question Structure + Visual Toolkit. Use as a menu, never as a quota.

families.name: Reading Check
families.primary_job: short conceptual comprehension / distinction / recognition after reading
families.bank_use: compact concept checks, terminology distinctions, immediate conceptual checkpoints

families.name: Think and Do
families.primary_job: observable action, small demonstration, sketch, measurement, or physical test
families.bank_use: phenomenon prompts, investigation seeds, concrete model checks

families.name: Plug and Chug
families.primary_job: straightforward use of a physical relationship after its meaning is established
families.bank_use: limited formula fluency and units; never let it replace conceptual modeling

families.name: Think and Solve
families.primary_job: quantitative application requiring selection/interpretation of a relationship
families.bank_use: multi-step quantitative reasoning with physical interpretation

families.name: Think and Rank
families.primary_job: rank/compare cases using diagrams, graphs, models, or proportional reasoning
families.bank_use: high-value Physics representation family; especially useful for vector, force, motion, energy, wave, optics, circuit, and field comparisons

families.name: Think and Explain
families.primary_job: conceptual synthesis, misconception resolution, causal explanation, or model critique
families.bank_use: original conceptual reasoning; explanation must arise from the physics job rather than a generic justify tail

families.name: Think and Discuss
families.primary_job: discussion-worthy conceptual tension, prediction, or competing explanation
families.bank_use: Stop-and-Discuss seeds and teacher discourse; not automatically an assessment item

hard_rules: Do not reproduce protected textbook question wording by default; adapt the reasoning architecture and author original prompts.
Think and Rank is a representation-rich family, not merely a verbal ranking list.
Plug and Chug follows conceptual meaning; it does not become the dominant course voice.
Question-family labels are authoring metadata and normally remain hidden from students.
